tasks.title: Robot posture joint states use an unregistered schema name

judge_tasks.title: Achieve stable, full-travel grip
judge_tasks.description: The planner must be updated to enforce full trigger travel (index finger pull reaching 90% of the trigger's range) and to incorporate a grip strategy that achieves stable opposition for the thumb and index finger, ensuring the tool does not slide or rotate during the 'drive' phase.
changes_to_try: Update the grip planner to prioritize 'full_trigger_travel' and 'thumb_opposes' features.

still_in_hand: PASS (rotation < 1.0 deg, slide < 0.5 mm)

judge_tasks.title: Restore Thumb Opposition, Clear Middle Finger from Trigger, and Achieve Full Trigger Pull
judge_tasks.description: Modify the tool_grip planner parameters so the hand grasps slightly lower and seated deeper at the web, allowing the middle finger to clear the trigger completely, the index finger to strike the trigger with better leverage to reach >= 90% travel without stalling, and the thumb to flex into the web concavity after the palm seats.
changes_to_try: Lower the hand slightly along the handle in tool_grip (e.g., shift along_m from -0.003 to -0.005 or -0.006 m and tighten finger_edge_m from -0.006 toward -0.002 m) so the middle finger stays strictly below the trigger guard and never contacts the trigger.

Replace thumb='off' with a delayed two-stage thumb closure (rotate thumb abduction into opposition and flex to >= 0.5 rad only after the approach/palm-seat phase completes) so the thumb wraps the narrow neck behind the trigger rather than striking the wide top barrel during approach.

Reduce palm_gap_m or adjust wrist yaw_deg/roll_deg (e.g., yaw_deg toward -15 or -20 deg) so the index proximal/middle phalanx contacts the trigger closer to the knuckle, increasing mechanical advantage against the 15 N trigger spring and keeping the handle back seated against the palm during axial drive.

tasks.title: Set the Forward/Reverse Switch (Rung 3)
tasks.description: The robot must set the forward/reverse switch (e.g., to 'forward') using the hand's thumb or index finger, and then pull the trigger to initiate the drive.
success_measures: The hand must physically manipulate the switch mechanism (e.g., a force sensor reading on the switch area).
The robot must maintain a stable grip (e.g., 'still_in_hand' > 0.95) while setting the switch.
The subsequent trigger pull must show the motor starting from a controlled, non-zero RPM (e.g., 'run_rpm' > 10 RPM) and maintaining it.
capabilities_needed: Fine motor control to manipulate small, discrete switches.
Ability to maintain grip stability while performing a secondary, non-linear action (setting the switch).
tasks.findings: tried 2026-10-17 with the holding hand's thumb (tool_grip_planner.thumb_switch_press, switch_body/switch_other_body): the switch's push-to-forward end is on the palm's side, but it sits in the corner under the barrel's overhang. Mapped over the thumb's whole joint space it comes within 0.2-0.6 mm of the end's face only at poses 8-20 mm inside the housing (one grip 2 mm, at the slicing's own error); a breadth-first search over (rotation, flex) from the grip's thumb found 95-206 clear poses for the three grips that reach the stage and none touching the switch. The Ability Hand's thumb (2.3-2.5 cm across) cannot reach it from the trigger grip. Next: the right hand pushes it while the left holds (a two-arm plan: the pick padded to 28 columns, a straight-line push like finger_push_planner's), or grips chosen for the switch as well as the trigger | Index probe 2026-10-17 (button_press_planner on the switch's 'direction' joint, the drill standing, switch centred): 451 index poses press part12's end face along +x with the hand clear of the drill - the barrel's overhang blocks the thumb, not a finger; the asset's switch has no detent (damping 5 N s/m), so a slow press takes a fraction of a newton and will not tip the standing drill. Every pose fails IK (16-32 mm, 23-41 deg): pushing toward forward points the LEFT index to the robot's right from the drill's left side. Next: a stance or drill pose (turned so the switch's left end faces the left hand) where the arm reaches it, then a pre-grasp press stage before the tool grip | 2026-10-17, the turned-drill route: scene aida_r5_dining_drill_switch (yaw -60, direction authored 0.0) - the index presses the switch on the standing drill (button_press, press_m 3.5 mm: 883 ticks, the law read forward from tick 699), then a tool_grip then-stage takes it up. The grip's then-plan failed (8 candidates, none with IK clear of the torso): its IK seeds were all scattered about the arm the press left (folded, the wrist rolled 120 deg). Each half alone planned (the live drill with the press's earlier arm; the authored drill with the live arm); seeded with the first stage's reset arm and the authored arm too it plans 1492 ticks. Rule: plan_er_grasp.then_request (tests/test_then_request.py), used by tool_then, door_then and screw_then
tasks.closed_why: 2026-10-17, aida_r5_dining_drill_switch (filmed): the index pressed the forward/reverse switch on the standing drill (direction 0 -> 1 at tick 699, switch_set_by_hand), the hand then took the drill up by its grip (TOOL_PLAN OK after then_request's seeds) and ran it: trigger 45 %, 289 rpm against the law's 288, stopped on release (1.5 rpm), held (drift 6.7 mm, still_in_hand 1.65 deg / 2.6 mm). Record cap rung 3 (no bit/workpiece: rung 4 is the drill-hole and screw scenes). Gemini placed it at rung 1: it judged the pre-grasp press unnatural (a person flips it in hand with the thumb - this hand's thumb cannot reach it, see findings) and wrongly said the trigger was never released (the log has the trigger to 0 and 477 -> 1.5 rpm in the release stage). Its in-hand reversal and full trigger range are its new rung-3 task. tasks.title: the drill hole wood interaction
tasks.description: a take in aida_r5_dining_drill_hole that passes hole.pass
tasks.findings: 2026-10-17 take 1 (aida_r5_dining_drill_hole, physics only): the grip, lift, looks and spin ran (bit 3.2 mm, 137 rpm at a third of the trigger); the hole started at the face (tilt 0.14 deg) but no wood was cut: the wall spring's damping read the tip's velocity as the link's linear velocity plus w x (tip - link origin) - this chuck's origin is the drill's, ~12 cm off the spin axis, so the tip read ~1.7 m/s sideways: the bit was kicked 7 mm off its line at the first touch and, back at the face, thrown out of the hand with the drill (the impact set the switch to reverse). Rule: material_laws.bit_reaction takes the tip's velocity from its position's change (tested); take 2 running | takes 2-3 (2026-10-17): with the tip's velocity its own, the drill stayed in the hand, but the hand never pushed the bit past ~6 N (take 2: 0.25 mm/rev, 1.5 mm lead) / 10.4 N (take 3: 0.15 mm/rev, 4 mm lead, no re-squeeze) against the 13.4 N a 3.2 mm bit needs to start cutting 710 kg/m3 plywood: as the arm pushes, the drill pitches back in the thumbless grip (1.7 -> 25 deg, 24 mm), the handle turns away from the index (15 -> 0 N on the trigger), the chuck stops (131 -> 0 rpm) and the bit walks 58 mm across the face. Take 2's re-squeeze dip let the index slam back at 39 N and kicked the bit out of its dimple (re-squeeze off for drilling; the wall now bears at most EN 1995's embedment strength x d x depth, then yields - tested). The geometry half is proven in PhysX on a DECLARED 3.2 mm hole (probe_hole.py: 2.9 mm peg through 18 mm, 4.2 mm peg stopped at the face; blind 10 mm: the peg stopped at 9.99 mm).
